I think we should just change implementation of scrolling to never rely on the state of the scrolled-in area:
- the abstract `grid_scroll` event leaves the state of the scrolled in area _undefined_. `screen.c` promises to to fill in the area with `grid_line` events before the next flush. 
- For a non-BCE terminal this makes redrawing _strictly_ more efficient. Instead of filling the entire area with spaces, and then drawing text on top, we just need to pad the unused area with spaces.
- For a BCE terminal we use ce or ec (the later not implemented yet) to pad each line. This mean one extra sequence per line at maximum, which should be acceptable. We then only rely on the BCE terminal implementing _explicit_ clearing sequences correctly, never implicit clearing with scrolling, newlines or anything.
- A GUI client can then implement `grid_scroll` as a single copy.

This also makes sense when considering `winhl=Normal:MyBackground` windows. For these windows the implicit clearing in `grid_scroll` is useless anyway, and the unused area needs to be cleared an extra time.

fwiw, terminal.app under macOS Yosemite 10.10 (old version, I know) tested with neovim 0.3.1 (the default `brew`) has background painting problems after `:colo`. It's probably both safe and not a performance issue to force a full repaint after the color scheme is changed.
"full repaint" is what the current code should do already when background color changes. Hard to investigate further with not at least a screenshot.

Sorry, I thought it did the repaint via BCE. It's the same as my typical BCE problem: cells without characters have the wrong background color. > Sorry, I thought it did the repaint via BCE. 

It _happens_ to be BCE-free on master, but for terminals that report BCE (and are not blacklisted), we could implement more efficient repainting that uses ce and ec.
See your "neovim 0.3.1" edit now, please try latest master. If it works on master there is nothing to fix..

Ok, I can confirm that the macOS 10.10 `colo` issue is gone in `master`. My point was that changing the colorscheme is not part of "normal" editor activity that needs to be optimized, and it would be better to err on the side of caution and not use ce/ec (as is now the case) rather than to do so.

I guess now that `master` is working here at least this is documented so that future efforts to optimizing background paint can know to be wary of this particular test case.

> and it would be better to err on the side of caution and not use ce/ec (as is now the case) rather than to do so.

Missing the point. `ce` is safe in "normal" operation if and only if it is safe when "repainting", the terminal emulator cannot care less. _Avoiding_ a special case for repainting is not somehow "unnecessary optimization", it is just avoiding a special case, and less opportunity for bugs in total. The _only_ way to fix BCE bugs is to detect which terminal support what operations correctly, not doing the same operation in multiple ways in the same terminal.
can this be closed?

There might still be the conhost issue. Based on the report, I think conhost implements the _implicit_ clearing of scrolling wrong, even if they support BCE for any explicit clearing operation (hence my suggestion of only relying on explicit clears). Still, a screenshot to confirm would be nice.

The only might was about Kity, under conhost the issue is 100% reproducible and affects all scroll (under `master` and Windows 10 18267).
